question.text: Per the current NISM V-A workbook (page 218), if an AMC fails to dispatch refund proceeds for a New Fund Offer within 5 business days from the closure of the NFO subscription list, what is the consequence?

answer.text: The AMC faces a one-time penalty from SEBI but no payment to the investor
The NFO is automatically cancelled and units already allotted are reversed
The AMC must pay interest at 15% per annum to the investor for the delayed period
The trustee must compensate the investor from the sponsor's contribution

explanation.text: The Logic: The current NISM V-A workbook (p.218) supports a 5-business-day NFO refund window and a 15% per annum interest payable by the AMC if refunds are delayed beyond that period. For redemption/repurchase proceeds, the workbook refers to the period specified by SEBI and to interest at the rate specified by SEBI — the legacy "10 business days" framing is no longer the current rule. The Trap: The penal interest is paid TO the investor, not to SEBI as a fine; the trustee is not the payer. The 10-business-day window for redemption proceeds is the older rule and is not supported by the current workbook page. Cross-Exam Context: NISM V-A and II-B both test NFO-refund and redemption-payout timelines and the 15% p.a. delay interest.
